slides.title: D3D-GEN: Robot-Aware Domain-Grounded Interactive 3D World Generation for Social Robotics
slides.tldr: AUTOMATED 3D WORLD GENERATION FOR SOCIAL ROBOTICS
slides.highlight: D3D-GEN uses a RAG pipeline to automate the creation of interactive 3D simulation environments, supporting the development of embodied AI for social navigation relevant to RwB.

card.one_liner: D3D-GEN generates interactive, robot-aware 3D worlds using a RAG pipeline grounded in autonomous domain research.
card.key_idea: An agent retrieves domain-specific constraints via web research to build a knowledge base, which guides LLM-based floorplan generation and semantic asset placement for simulators.
card.evaluation: Generated 450 worlds across residential, office, and hospital domains; outperformed baselines in object density, visual quality, and VQA accuracy via Gemini-based metrics.
card.limitation: Relies on an existing 3D asset database, which may not be available for every target domain.

slides.title: Study Explores Impact on Trust When Expressive Humanoid Robots Make Mistakes
slides.tldr: TRUST IMPACT OF HUMANOID ROBOT ERRORS
slides.highlight: This study examines how expressive humanoid robots affect human trust when mistakes occur, which is relevant to RwB's focus on human-robot interaction.

slides.title: Locomotion Variability and User Experience in Smart Wheelchair Human-Robot Interaction
slides.highlight: This research demonstrates that preserving natural movement variability in shared control for smart wheelchairs improves perceived agency and usefulness. It is relevant to RwB's focus on human-robot interaction and embodied learning.

card.one_liner: Preserving natural movement variability in smart wheelchair assistance improves user agency and experience without compromising performance.
card.key_idea: An autonomy-supportive shared control strategy using an inverted bell-shaped variability factor to minimize assistance in task-irrelevant areas while maintaining guidance at task-critical points.
card.evaluation: User study with 18 participants pushing an intelligent powered wheelchair; measured via ANOVA on trajectory variance, endpoint error, and Likert-scale questionnaires.

slides.title: HUI360: A 360° Egocentric Dataset and Baselines for Human-Robot Interaction Anticipation
slides.highlight: This work introduces HUI360, a large-scale egocentric dataset for anticipating human intentions, which supports the development of proactive and socially aware behavior for embodied agents in RwB.

card.one_liner: HUI360 is the largest in-the-wild 360° egocentric dataset for anticipating human-robot physical interactions.
card.key_idea: An automated pipeline using YOLOv11x, SAM2.1-L, and ViTPose/Sapiens to detect, track, and annotate interactions based on mask intersection with robot zones.
card.evaluation: Evaluated RF, MLP, and LSTM baselines using AUC, F1, and AP across cross-dataset and cross-environment transfers; LSTM performed best.
card.limitation: Focuses only on physical interactions, ignoring nuanced social signals like gaze, hesitation, or verbal engagement.

slides.title: Leading-Silence Augmentation and Multi-Stage Synthetic Supervision for the Second MLC-SLM Challenge
slides.highlight: This work addresses speaker diarization and recognition in unsegmented multilingual conversations, contributing to HyECHO's focus on identity recognition and diarization.

card.one_liner: Improves multilingual conversational speech diarization and understanding using leading-silence augmentation and synthetic QA supervision.
card.key_idea: Task 1 uses random leading-silence cropping and EMA training on VibeVoice-ASR-7B. Task 2 uses Qwen3-Omni-30B fine-tuned on synthetic QA pairs filtered for audio-dependency and distribution-matched.
card.evaluation: Task 1 tcpMER reduced from 18.30% to 16.73%. Task 2 accuracy increased from 78.0% to 86.0% on the challenge evaluation set.
card.limitation: Task 1 results lack per-language analysis and do not establish robustness to turn-boundary errors.

slides.title: DuplexWorld: Can voice agents help you get through the day?
slides.highlight: This work introduces DuplexWorld to evaluate voice agents across diverse conversational scenarios, providing insights into turn-taking and conversational capabilities relevant to HyECHO's focus on social perception.

card.one_liner: DuplexWorld benchmarks voice agents across six diverse worlds, revealing a gap between conversational fluency and task completion.
card.key_idea: A holistic evaluation suite using 156 scenarios across six worlds (enterprise and navigation) measuring agentic capability, conversational dynamics, and speech naturalness via a unified tick-based harness.
card.evaluation: Evaluated five commercial S2S systems using 3,825 conversations. Metrics include Pass@1, turn-taking, and DNSMOS. Results show the best agent achieved Pass@1 of 0.490.
card.limitation: The benchmark uses simulated users rather than real human audio for its evaluations.

slides.title: Seeing Machines Launches Physical AI Platform for Humanoid Robots
slides.tldr: PHYSICAL AI PLATFORM FOR HUMANOID ROBOTS
slides.highlight: The launch of a Physical AI Platform for humanoid robots provides relevant technological developments for RwB's focus on embodied social robots.

slides.title: Robust Multi-Tier Infant-Centered Audio Understanding with Whisper via Structured Speaker Conditioning
slides.highlight: This work introduces a multi-tier audio tagger using speaker conditioning to handle noise and domain shifts in home environments, supporting HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception and identity recognition.

card.one_liner: A multi-tier audio tagging framework using LoRA-finetuned Whisper for infant-centered naturalistic recordings in home environments.
card.key_idea: Combines a Whisper encoder with a target-speaker Transformer using factorized speaker tokens (shared tier token + family-specific offset) and a sequence-level temporal smoothing loss.
card.evaluation: Tested on 17 hours of audio from 52 families using Macro-F1 and Kappa; outperformed TL-TR and W2V-LB baselines across all tiers.
card.limitation: Unsupervised test-time adaptation for unseen families yielded only modest improvements, indicating a need for more robust personalization mechanisms.

slides.title: FlowLOB: Efficient and Controllable Limit Order Book Generation with Flow Matching
slides.tldr: EFFICIENT LIMIT ORDER BOOK GENERATION VIA FLOW MATCHING
slides.highlight: FlowLOB utilizes flow-matching to generate realistic and controllable limit order book trajectories, contributing to the simulation of complex market dynamics relevant to MIMIC's societal-scale modeling.

card.one_liner: FlowLOB uses flow matching to generate realistic, controllable limit order book trajectories with high sampling efficiency.
card.key_idea: A conditional flow-matching generator using an adaLN-Zero transformer and tick-relative representation to enable multi-symbol training and zero-shot transfer to unseen instruments.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on HKEX data against agent-based and learned baselines using Wasserstein-1, KS, KL, and JS distances; results show superior realism at high frequencies.
card.limitation: Performance degrades at coarser sampling frequencies (10s), where it fails to dominate marginal metrics and exhibits less reliable trend control.
